title: llama.cpp v1.0 promises a stable C API. A break will change the major version.
friendlyTitle: llama.cpp version 1.0 is a promise about what will break.
summary: On 13 November, the llama.cpp project released library version 1.0.0 for llama.cpp and for ggml. The point is not a new model. It is a versioning promise. A breaking change to the public C API in the include directory will now raise the major version. A compatible feature, backend update, or new model support raises the minor version. A bug fix with no API change is a patch. The project says it currently supports more than 150 architecture variants.
friendlySummary: On 13 November, the llama.cpp project released version 1.0.0 of its libraries. This is not a new model. It is a promise about changes. If the public programming interface breaks, the first version number will change. A new feature that still works with old programs changes the middle number. A bug fix changes the last number. The project says it supports more than 150 kinds of model.
whyItMatters: If you ship an app on llama.cpp, a major bump is now the signal that your build may break. Prebuilt artifacts cover Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, and iOS. Packages also go out through Docker, Debian, Homebrew, conda-forge, MacPorts, Winget, and an XCFramework for Apple platforms. The same post points to Llama desktop apps for macOS and Windows. It does not announce a Linux desktop app. Yesterday's trending-repo note was about the project climbing GitHub. This is the stability promise.
